thread:
katie: Quick sync — I'm consolidating the tool-calling examples across the SDK pages and adding a small smoke-test suite that runs in docs CI. Want to align on ✅ what to keep, what to redirect, and a deprecation note for older snippets.

ravi: SGTM. Can you sketch the migration plan? need to know which PRs i'll review.

katie: Plan v1: 1) pick canonical examples (one minimal, one robust) for both Python and JS; 2) replace duplicated snippets with include links; 3) add smoke tests that run the example with mocked tool responses; 4) add redirect page for legacy examples + deprecation banner.

miguel: For the smoke tests, can we just run the examples with `--dry-run` env var instead of full mocks? simpler for CI.

lena: Dry-run is fine for simple snippets but we need at least one e2e where function/tool calling receives a sample JSON response to validate schema parsing. otherwise we miss regressions.

sam: +1 to lena. we already had a bug where the SDK parsing dropped `metadata` in nested objects. a real small mock will catch that.

katie: Good call. Proposal: two smoke tests per example set — dry-run for lint/style + a tiny mock-based e2e for parsing. Keep them < 10s each.

josh: Where will the mocks live? inline fixtures or separate testdata dir?

katie: separate `docs/testdata/toolcall_fixtures/` so multiple examples can reference the same payload. less duplication.

ravi: For canonical examples, can we standardize on this shape: request includes `tools: [{name,input_schema}]`, model returns `tool_call` with `name` and `arguments` as a JSON string. We should show both raw and parsed usage.

miguel: Yes show both. Example snippet idea:

```python
# minimal: raw tool call handling
def handle_resp(resp):
    if resp.get("tool_call"):
        payload = json.loads(resp["tool_call"]["arguments"])
        print(payload["result"])
```

katie: Nice. We'll need to ensure the JS SDK snippet mirrors that pattern. Also add a short note about schema-first vs ad-hoc parsing.

lena: About redirects — we have ~7 legacy pages that many customers link to. I'll compile a list and add permanent redirects with a short note of why (examples consolidated).

sam: Also flag internal OSS mirrors; one partner sync pinged earlier about broken links in their guide. we should include `X-Docs-Redirect: 1` header example for partners.

katie: Good point. I'll add a small section in the migration doc with a curl example for partners:

```bash
curl -I https://docs.redwood.ai/old/toolcall -H "X-Docs-Redirect: 1"
```

ravi: PR plan? i'll take canonical examples and smoke tests for python. miguel will do JS examples and mock harness. katie will handle redirects + migration writeup. lena will compile link list. sam will run partner outreach for link updates. josh will review CI integration.

josh: FYI docs-ci will block if any snippet fails the smoke e2e. we should keep timeouts reasonable.

docs-ci: Test run queued: docs/smoke/toolcall (python) — expected duration 8s.

katie: I'll open PRs as small pieces: 1) add canonical examples + fixtures, 2) add smoke CI job, 3) deprecation/redirect pages + redirects file. linking each PR in the migration doc.

miguel: One more tiny ask — add a short compatibility paragraph in each example: "If you use older SDK v0.x, call `.toJSON()` on `arguments`" (or whatever compatibility shim). avoids customer confusion.

katie: Yup. We'll include a 1-line compatibility hint and a pointer to a changelog entry.

lena: I'll drop the legacy link list into the PR description so redirects can be added in the same commit. saves churn.

sam: livesync: do we want a redirect TTL / date for the deprecation banner? recommended: 90 days then hard-removal note.

katie: Let's do 90 days. migration doc will include the timeline and contact points.

ravi: ETA? can we aim for the docs release on Tue?

katie: Targeting next Tuesday. I'll have PR #1 today, others by Friday. reviewers: @ravi @josh @lena.

miguel: I'll start the JS snips and add a small GitHub Actions job to run the Node smoke test.

josh: I'll add the new job to the `.github/workflows/docs-ci.yml` but gate it behind `docs-smoke` label until it's stable.

docs-ci: docs/smoke/toolcall (python) — PASS  (8.3s) :white_check_mark:

katie: Lovely. i'll push the first PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421 — PTAL when you have a moment.

ravi: Looking. if we keep snippets under 12 lines each, they render nicely in the callouts.

sam: Also add one health-check note in the SDK README pointing to these canonical examples. helps adoption.

katie: Added to checklist. thanks everyone :rocket:

miguel: quick follow-up — should we include a tiny `invalid-json` fallback snippet showing graceful errors? customers trip on that.

lena: Yes show a pattern: try/except + fallback to tool-run. one line.

katie: Added to the snippet list. closing loop once PRs are up.
